title: Cellular Senescence Genes as Cutting-Edge Signatures for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Diagnosis: Potential for Innovative Therapeutic Interventions.
authors: Zhang, Shuli; Li, Jiayin; Wang, Ruichen; Zhao, Xiaojie; Mei, Zhu; Wang, Xiaozeng
journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
one_liner_zh: 该文研究腹主动脉瘤中细胞衰老相关基因的诊断标志物，属于纯转录组与湿实验验证，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合建模及AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is the most prevalent dilated arterial aneurysm that poses a significant threat to older adults, but the molecular mechanisms linking senescence to AAA progression remain poorly understood. This study aims to identify cellular senescence-related genes (SRGs) implicated in AAA development and assess their potential as therapeutic targets. Four hundred and twenty-nine differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified from the GSE57691 training set, and 867 SRGs were obtained. Through the intersection of DEGs with SRGs, 19 differentially expressed senescence-related genes (DESRGs) were uncovered. Functional enrichment analysis was performed to explore their biological roles in AAA. To identify hub genes, we applied machine learning algorithms, including LASSO, SVM-RFE and random forest. These hub genes were then validated in two independent datasets. In the initial validation cohort, significant differences in the expression levels of BTG2, ETS1, ID1 and ITPR3 were observed between the AAA and control groups. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated a robust diagnostic performance. Further validation across different AAA stages (small, large and ruptured AAA) identified ETS1 and ITPR3 as potential diagnostic genes. Subsequently, the diagnostic relevance of ETS1 and ITPR3 was further validated in human serum samples and mouse models of AAA. In addition, single-cell RNA sequencing suggests that senescent endothelial cells play a pivotal role in AAA progression, we further confirmed the correlation between ETS1 and ITPR3 and senescent endothelial cells by WB, IF and RT-qPCR. In conclusion, our study reveals the pivotal role of cellular senescence in AAA progression and identifies ETS1 and ITPR3 as promising diagnostic biomarkers.
abstract_zh: 腹主动脉瘤（AAA）是最常见的扩张性动脉瘤，对老年人构成重大威胁，但将衰老与AAA进展联系起来的分子机制仍知之甚少。本研究旨在识别与AAA发展相关的细胞衰老相关基因（SRGs），并评估其作为治疗靶点的潜力。从GSE57691训练集中识别出429个差异表达基因（DEGs），并获取了867个SRGs。通过将DEGs与SRGs取交集，发现了19个差异表达衰老相关基因（DESRGs）。进行了功能富集分析以探索它们在AAA中的生物学作用。为识别核心基因，我们应用了机器学习算法，包括LASSO、SVM-RFE和随机森林。随后，这些核心基因在两个独立数据集中得到验证。在初始验证队列中，观察到BTG2、ETS1、ID1和ITPR3在AAA组与对照组之间的表达水平存在显著差异。受试者工作特征（ROC）分析显示出稳健的诊断性能。进一步在不同AAA阶段（小型、大型和破裂AAA）的验证中，将ETS1和ITPR3识别为潜在诊断基因。随后，ETS1和ITPR3的诊断相关性在人类血清样本和小鼠AAA模型中进一步得到验证。此外，单细胞RNA测序提示衰老内皮细胞在AAA进展中发挥关键作用，我们通过WB、IF和RT-qPCR进一步确认了ETS1和ITPR3与衰老内皮细胞之间的相关性。总之，我们的研究揭示了细胞衰老在AAA进展中的关键作用，并将ETS1和ITPR3识别为有前景的诊断生物标志物。
